subject: xspark1
label: sprites/xspark1.spr, in the place of the game's own

againstClass.words: flickers: more coherence from frame to frame

R1.reason: Each of the nine frames is one soft glowing disc, a bright white core in a blue halo on a dark ground, which is the light of an electric spark as the brief describes. No frame shows anything else.

R2.reason: Frames are 32 by 32 as the original's are. The glow sits centred and its halo fades out well inside the edges; the measured border is 0, so nothing is clipped or hard-edged at the frame's border.

R3.reason: By eye the colour is the brief's: white-hot core and a blue-white halo across all nine frames. Brightness varies slightly from frame to frame, but the hue holds.

R4.reason: The loop closes (wrap 0.96, inside the class range) and the envelope holds at both ends (first and last 0.97, inside 0.57 to 1), so the loop and fade-in/out are right. Frame-to-frame jitter is 1.98, above the fire loop class's range of 1.33 to 1.79, so the flicker is too erratic compared with Half-Life's own. Frames 1 and 5 also show small uneven specks in the halo. The frame count (9) is not checked against a class figure here.

R5.reason: Type parallel and format additive match the game's file (gameType parallel, gameFormat additive). The name is the same, and it reads back as written.
